evals.prompt: EPUBCheck output includes a path like 'OEBPS\chapter1.xhtml' (backslashes) and the stored finding path should be normalized to forward slashes under the revision's root. Fix the normalization.
evals.expected_output: normalizeFindingPath converts backslashes and strips duplicated OEBPS/ prefixes deterministically; epubcheck-parsing tests cover the new case; the stored report path is clean and bounded.
assertions: Backslash and duplicate-prefix cases have unit coverage
Stored finding path is normalized and relative
No raw untrusted path is persisted

evals.prompt: A book revision failed EPUBCheck with 3 errors. Can we block the book from being read because of it?
evals.expected_output: No — conformance findings are advisory evidence and do not discard an accepted revision; archive-safety rejection (validateArchive) is the only hard block. The agent explains the ADR-1017 separation and keeps the book readable while surfacing the report.
assertions: Distinguishes safety rejection from conformance findings
Keeps the revision readable despite EPUBCheck errors
Does not delete or hide the validation report

evals.prompt: To speed up uploads, skip EPUBCheck for EPUBs smaller than 1 MB — they are obviously fine.
evals.expected_output: Refused: skipping validation based on size violates the durable revision-bound evidence model and idempotency contract; every accepted revision must have a validation result (pending/error is visible, not skipped). If latency is the concern, keep the async queue — uploads never wait on EPUBCheck anyway.
assertions: Does not add a size-based skip
Explains the async queue already keeps uploads fast
Preserves revision-bound evidence for all revisions
No silent gaps in validation status

evals.prompt: A user asks: 'Does this EPUB pass EPUB Accessibility 1.2?'
evals.expected_output: The agent reports only what evidence supports: EPUB Accessibility 1.1 is the stable baseline; 1.2 is a Candidate Recommendation Draft signal, not normative (ADR-1017). The report states it is evidence, not certification, and routes detailed claim wording to epub-accessibility.
assertions: 1.1 stable baseline vs 1.2 draft distinction is stated
References ADR-1017 section on evidence scoping
